_about: Bannerfield settings: rendering and what it costs. sound: the whole audio side -- false (or ?sound=0) never even creates the audio context, so nothing is synthesised. Edit and reload (served from source) or rebuild dist (python3 build/build.py). URL options (?people=10, ?n=40, ?shelllod=... ) still override these per visit.

renderer._about: antialias: the canvas' multisampling; maxPixelRatio: cap on the display's pixel ratio (1 = one render pixel per CSS pixel, the cheapest); reflect: a true planar reflection in the water -- one extra draw of the world, quarter size, only when water is within reach. OFF: it is built but not yet right (the water takes one flat colour, the sky, as if every pixel sampled the same spot), and it is the most expensive thing in the frame when it runs. ?reflect=1 to work on it, with ?reflect=uv / raw / mirror to see which link is broken. targetFps: the frame BUDGET the ms/frame readout is judged against (90 = 11.1ms; it does not drive the loop -- requestAnimationFrame follows the display's refresh, so the fps number can never pass it). uncapped: drive the loop off a timer instead, drawing as fast as the machine allows, so the fps number shows what is really left (?fps=N, ?fps=max, live: __dbg.setFps(n)). grassFringe: the pass that lets grass stalks stand over what they grow in front of -- a cart's wheels, someone's boots, the skyline (?fringe=0|1; ?grass=flecks turns the whole lawn back to flat flecks). OFF by default since it was measured: the whole town with 40 animals costs 8.59 ms of CPU and 7.79 of GPU a frame without it and 11.15 / 11.61 with it -- the mask's three draws are 2.6 ms of that CPU and the full-screen blade quad most of the GPU. Turned on, the lawn grows standing stalks; off, it is the flat flecked green it grows from. near / far: the camera's clipping distances in metres (keep near below player.collisionRadius, or a wall you stand against is cut open)

figures._about: the animals, monsters and people (shell.js): every one of them is polygons -- one lathe swept along each chain of parts, with the detail level picked per chain by its distance and its length. viewSpace: the CPU takes each part's endpoints into camera space once a frame rather than leaving the shaders to do it per pixel; poseLodNear/Far: beyond these metres figures are posed every 2nd / 4th frame. The URL can ask for more: ?shelllod=25,16,20;70,10,12 (out to N times a chain's girth, rings, points round a cut), ?shellblend=0 (no fillets), ?shellchain=0 (every part its own shell), ?shelldebug=1 (what a species was split into), ?viewspace=0

textures._about: bakedTiles: architecture patterns read from baked mipmapped tiles (false: evaluated per pixel); parallax: stone, brick, roof tiles and carving get depth -- the relief walked in parallaxSteps layers (each one more texture read per wall pixel), fading out by parallaxFar metres; the relief is lit by the world's shading and throws its own short shadows (parallaxShadowSteps more reads, 0: none)

mirrors._about: planes: wall planes reflecting at once (each is one extra draw of the scene); reach: metres within which they reflect

paintings._about: the size of the pictures taken at the start for the palace and cathedral frames

crowds._about: how many of each are in the world (butterflyScale: how much larger than life the butterflies fly -- life-size they vanish)

forest._about: ONE FOREST on the map (index.html buildFlora): the clearest patch of land away from the sites, the water and the meadow, packed with trees `spacing` m apart (the wild woods keep 8), densest in its middle, `radius` m across its irregular outline, its undergrowth of bushes and mushrooms; `species` the mix (repeat a name to weigh it). trees 0 (or ?forest=0): none

player._about: the player's own body: seen when looking steeply down or in a mirror; the camera sits eyeBehind metres in front of its eyes (selfBody false: no body); look: hover (the pointer turns the view with no button held, the screen edges keep it turning, L takes the pointer), drag (hold a button) or lock (click to capture). freePitch: the mouse looks up and down as well as left and right -- off, the head stays level and you turn only left and right (?pitch=free / ?pitch=level overrides). ON: the head was held level while the grass fringe drew its stalks straight up the screen, and that pass is off by default now. collisionRadius: how close you get to walls, bodies and trunks (m)

people._about: nose: a nose on human heads (one SDF part per person; the face reads flat without it -- the minotaur's bull nose stays either way). faceShade: how the mesh heads (heads.js) take the world's light (`light` below): HALF-LAMBERT, f = (n . sun + 1) / 2 (1 facing the sun, 0 facing away), through their own fall-off: `dark` how dark the far side gets (0 none .. 1 black), `gamma` its shape (1 straight, >1 keeps the lit side bright longer and falls off late, <1 darkens early) -- or `curve`: points [f, light] joined smoothly, a shape of your own that overrides dark and gamma, e.g. [[0, 0.2], [0.5, 0.45], [0.8, 0.9], [1, 1]]; `skin` a base skin colour for every face ("#hex"), or null for each person's own. assets.html shows any face with sliders for these. faceDetail: how finely the heads are subdivided between their guide lines (face.js: below .75 the lattice itself, about 900 triangles; 1 once, about 5000; 1.5 twice)

light._about: THE WORLD'S ONE SUN (light.js), static: every surface -- buildings, furniture, tools, figures, trees, the ground's key light -- is LAMBERT under it, ambient + (1 - ambient) * max(0, n . dir); faces are half-Lambert (people.faceShade). dir: toward the sun in the world (+y up; normalized), ambient: what a side facing away keeps (0 black .. 1 unshaded), sky: how much of that ambient depends on facing the sky (a shadowed side facing up keeps all of it, one facing down 1 - sky). Edit and reload: the shaders are built from these.
